newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-SHINE WRAPS UP STUNNING SOMERST VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SHINE WRAPS UP STUNNING SOMERST VICTORY.

text.p: Fast bowler Kevin Shine completed an 11-wicket match haul as Somerset raced to a stunning victory over Lancashire inside two days in the English County Championship on Thursday.
Shine finished with his best-ever match figures for the county, collecting four for 54 in Lancashire's second innings of 164, to finish with 11 for 97 in the match.
Chasing 64 runs for their first win of the season, Somerset secured the seven-wicket victory before the close, after rain had washed out the first session.
Derbyshire's Adrian Rollins hit his second double century of his career and a best ever 210 as his side reached 523 in their first innings against Hampshire.
Rollins, resuming on 151 at the start of play, and Paul Aldred (83) put on 149 for the eighth wicket.
Hampshire's Jason Laney (61) and Australian Matthew Hayden (46) compiled an opening stand of 110, before they both fell to Andrew Harris. Hampshire were 166 for two at the close.
Ally Brown (109) carried Surrey to a first innings total of 280 after Essex had made 347 in their first knock.
Ashley Cowan took five for 58 for Essex who had progressed to 40 without loss in their second innings at the close.
Former England batsmen Mike Gatting (94) and Mark Ramprakash (97) carried Middlesex to 298 for four against county champions Leicestershire at Lord's.
Earlier, Leicestershire were dismissed for 280 with another former England player Angus Fraser finishing with six for 77.
At Northampton, Nottinghamshire took a first innings lead against Northamptonshire, moving to 259 for nine in reply to Northants's 235 all out.
Kent also grabbed a first innings advantage when they moved 319 for eight, after Warwickshire had made 314 the first time around.
Gloucestershire took control of their match against Yorkshire, building an overall lead of 303 after moving to 281 for five in their second innings at the close.
At Chester-le-Street, Durham were 309 for nine, after Sussex had made 373 in their first innings.
